rationale: Acceptance did not run (no spec/story artifact), so decision_needed is unavailable and confidence is capped low; blind, edge-case and verification-gap lenses all ran with parseable, real findings, and standards (coverage_gap: false) found two commit-format violations now carried as CR-001/CR-002. 7 blocking findings survive triage (5 code, 2 standards). 4 candidates were dismissed after reachability checks: a cosmetic 95%-summing column-width report, a double-invocation concern already guarded by Checker's own disabled state, a catalog-cache merge pattern the test suite confirms is intentional, and the missing x-user-mcp-auth-location login-prompt handling (edge-case + verification-gap duplicate), which the original task explicitly scopes out ('No auth-required handling anywhere, these MCP servers have no user sign-in'). No findings deferred.

standards_review.notes: 20 of 22 commit subjects in range match 'EPMCDME-XXXX: Capital sentence'; two do not (see CR-001, CR-002).
No code-quality.md guide exists in the repo and no code_quality ArtifactRef was passed.

No new dangerouslySetInnerHTML/innerHTML, message listeners, window.location navigation, env reads, or nosonar markers in any changed file; the one open-redirect-relevant URL sink (broker login popup) was removed during consolidation, so no unsafe sink remains.

findings.title: Non-conforming commit subject casing
findings.problem: Commit subject 'EPMCDME-15541: implement integrations for admin mcp capability testing' has a lowercase first word after the ticket colon, violating git-workflow.md's 'EPMCDME-XXXX: Capital sentence' format.
findings.impact: Tekton CI's commit-message regex blocks the pipeline on this subject.
findings.recommendation: Reword to 'EPMCDME-15541: Implement integrations for admin mcp capability testing' (the squash-merge subject must also conform).

findings.title: Commit subject missing ticket-prefixed format
findings.problem: Commit subject 'epmcdme-15541-mcp-test-capability: add planning artifacts' uses a lowercase, hyphenated non-ticket prefix instead of 'EPMCDME-15541:', with a lowercase first word.
findings.impact: Tekton CI's commit-message regex blocks the pipeline on this subject.

findings.title: Unknown last_test_status renders as Not tested
findings.problem: In MCPLastTestBadge, `(status && BADGE_CONFIG[status]) || NOT_TESTED` falls back to the 'Not tested' badge whenever the backend returns a last_test_status value outside 'success'|'failure'|'warning', even though the caller has already passed MCPLastTestInfo's `!status` guard and is rendering the test timestamp/message alongside it.
findings.impact: An admin sees a contradictory state: a last-tested timestamp and message next to a badge claiming the server was never tested, hiding that a test actually ran and masking any new backend status value.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit fallback for a truthy-but-unrecognized status (e.g. StatusEnum.Warning with the raw status text) instead of silently matching the no-status case.

findings.title: last_test_error_category fetched but never displayed
findings.problem: last_test_error_category is added to MCPConfig and LAST_TEST_KEYS (fetched and merged on every test), but MCPLastTestInfo only renders last_test_message — the category is never surfaced.
findings.impact: Admins troubleshooting a failed test lose the structured error category the backend returns and must rely on the free-text message only; the added test only asserts the message renders, so this gap would recur unnoticed.
findings.recommendation: Render last_test_error_category in MCPLastTestInfo's failure/warning branch, or drop it from LAST_TEST_KEYS if intentionally deferred.

findings.title: Warning test result shown as success in Checker
findings.problem: runTest's modal status mapping is `result.last_test_status === 'failure' ? FAILED : SUCCESS`, so a 'warning' result (handled distinctly by reportResult's toaster.info branch two lines earlier) sets the Checker to SUCCESS.
findings.impact: The modal's Checker button shows a green success check for a run the toaster simultaneously reports as a warning, giving the admin two contradictory signals from the same test.
findings.recommendation: Map 'warning' to a distinct, non-SUCCESS Checker state mirroring the three-way branch already used in reportResult.

findings.title: Details panel vanishes silently when its config leaves the list
findings.problem: detailsServer is derived live via `configs.find(...)`; if the backing config is dropped from configs (pagination change, filter, list refresh) while the details panel is open, detailsServer becomes null with no explicit close or message.
findings.impact: The details sidebar disappears without explanation while the admin is viewing it, reading as a UI glitch rather than an intentional close.
findings.recommendation: When the live lookup misses, either retain the last-known server snapshot for display or close the panel explicitly with a notice rather than letting it vanish.

findings.title: mergeLastTest can blank previously-shown last-test fields
findings.problem: mergeLastTest unconditionally sets every LAST_TEST_KEYS field to result[key] from the new test response; if a response omits a field the UI currently displays (e.g. last_test_integration_alias on a run without one), that field is overwritten with undefined instead of preserved or explicitly cleared.
findings.impact: A previously-shown last-test detail can silently disappear from the UI after a later test run that doesn't return it, with no indication the data was dropped versus genuinely absent.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the backend always returns the full LAST_TEST_KEYS set on every test response; if a field can legitimately be omitted, merge with `key in result ? result[key] : merged[key]` instead of unconditional assignment.
